name: Côte de Nuits

known.via: English Wikipedia "Côte de Nuits" (a wine place on Wikidata)

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.
keyfacts: Six of its communes produce Grand Cru wines: Gevrey-Chambertin, Morey-Saint-Denis, Chambolle-Musigny, Vougeot, Flagey-Échezeaux and Vosne-Romanée.
There are 24 Grand Cru vineyards clustered around six villages, and more than 100 Premier Cru vineyards across the region.

notes: Gevrey-Chambertin, Morey-Saint-Denis and Vougeot are noted for full bodied reds.
Chambolle-Musigny's chalky soils give lighter bodied wines with finer aromas.

blurb.text: The northern part of the Côte d'Or, from Dijon to just south of Nuits-Saint-Georges. It is best known for reds made from Pinot Noir. Six of its communes produce Grand Cru wines.
